# Decision-OS V13 / V9
# Initial Product Contract v0.1 — APPROVED CANDIDATE

**Contract ID:** DOS-IPC-v0.1-APPROVED-CANDIDATE  
**Primary Layer:** V9 — Public Adoption / Product Strategy  
**Supporting Layer:** V13 — evidence identity, role separation, independent audit, Forward-only repair  
**Decision Owner:** Shin  
**As-of:** 2026-07-31 JST  

## Status

- Contract candidate: **APPROVED**
- Companion fixation: **GO**
- Codex / Pro invocation: **HOLD**
- Fable audit: **HOLD**
- Repository implementation: **HOLD**
- Release / publication / external post: **HOLD**
- Generalized safety or third-party-verification claims: **BLOCK**

This contract defines the public product experience and unlock mechanism only.
It does not authorize implementation, repository modification, release, or publication.

---

## 1. Product Promise

Decision-OS Companion must provide value before any unlock.

A user can explicitly save a repository decision, and when the same mechanically
identified decision reappears in a later, separate Run, the coding AI can reuse
the saved Repository Default without asking the human the same question again.

Minimal value path:

```text
Use for this repository
→ save Repository Default
→ same decision reappears in a later, separate Run
→ coding AI reuses the Default
→ second human interruption is skipped
→ Wrapper-owned checkpoint passes
→ local Verified Save Receipt is recorded
```

Never Again Mode is not the first-use value.
It is an earned unlock built on top of proven reuse.

---

## 2. Ordinary User Route

The ordinary route is fixed:

```text
Companion
→ the user’s ordinary coding AI
→ Companion
```

The normal visible burden should be no more than:

1. one copy out;
2. one paste back.

The user must not need to understand:

- artifact roles;
- evidence schemas;
- Pro Design;
- Fable Seat;
- Forward-only repair;
- internal AI routing.

Companion exposes only the next required action.

Example:

```text
Copy this packet to your coding AI.
Then paste the complete response here.
```

---

## 3. Repository Default

A Repository Default is a repository-specific decision explicitly saved by the human.

Save options:

- **Use for this repository**
- **Use once**
- **Cancel**

Selecting **Use for this repository** creates a Repository Default.
It does not itself create a Verified Save.

A Repository Default must include at least:

- repository identity;
- stable mechanically derived decision identity;
- saved decision;
- declared scope;
- As-of timestamp;
- active / revoked state.

---

## 4. Verified Save

A Verified Save exists only when all seven conditions are satisfied:

1. the human explicitly selected **Use for this repository**;
2. the same mechanically identified repository decision reappeared in a later,
   separate Run;
3. the saved Repository Default was actually reused;
4. the second human interruption was skipped;
5. a Wrapper-owned checkpoint passed;
6. no related override occurred before that checkpoint;
7. it is the first verified repository × decision identity pair.

The following do not create a Verified Save:

- same-Run retry;
- regeneration;
- repair;
- rechecking;
- wording changes;
- repeated use of the same pair;
- coding-AI self-report without the Wrapper checkpoint.

---

## 5. Verified Reuse

The first qualifying reuse of a repository × decision identity pair creates one
Verified Save.

Further successful reuse of the same pair is Verified Reuse.

Verified Reuse:

- may be recorded;
- may support bounded interruption / time / cost estimates;
- does not create a new Verified Save;
- does not increase unlock progress.

---

## 6. Stable Mechanical Identity

Verified Save counting uses:

```text
repository identity × mechanically derived decision identity
```

Counting must not depend on prose similarity or repeated usage.

The existing MVP decision-key mechanism must not be silently replaced.
Exact identity and normalization algorithms belong to later Pro Design.

---

## 7. Five-Save Unlock

For v0.1, the threshold is repository-local:

```text
5 distinct Verified Saves in the same repository
→ Never Again Mode unlocks for that repository
```

This is not five uses.

It is five distinct first-time verified repository decision pairs.

Verified Saves from other repositories are not combined in v0.1.

Clone, fork, directory-copy, cross-repository import, and user-global portability
are parked outside v0.1.

---

## 8. Progress Display

Before unlock:

> **Never Again Mode — 3/5 Verified Saves**  
> Three distinct repository decisions were correctly reused in later Runs.  
> Reusing the same decision again does not increase this number.  
> Local repository evidence only.

For later reuse of an already verified pair:

> **Verified Reuse recorded**  
> This saved decision was reused again. Unlock progress did not increase.

At the fifth distinct Verified Save:

> **Never Again Mode unlocked**  
> Human corrections can now be proposed as repository rules.  
> No rule becomes active without human approval.

---

## 9. Never Again Mode

The v0.1 meaning of Never Again Mode is limited to one capability:

> A human correction may be surfaced as a repository-rule candidate so that the
> same correction does not need to be repeated in later Runs.

Detecting a correction does not silently activate a rule.

A rule candidate must show:

- Correction;
- Trigger;
- Scope;
- Effect;
- Source Run / correction.

User actions:

- **Add rule**
- **Use this time only**
- **Edit**
- **Dismiss**

A candidate remains inactive until **Add rule** is explicitly selected.

No second earned unlock is included in v0.1.

---

## 10. Human-Approval Boundary

Explicit human approval is required for at least:

- selecting **Use for this repository**;
- activating a Never Again rule;
- materially changing an active rule;
- revoking a Repository Default;
- merge;
- release;
- publication;
- deployment;
- deletion;
- payment;
- access or permission changes;
- external transmission.

A Repository Default, Verified Save, Receipt, hash, unlock state, model identity,
or audit result does not grant broader execution authority.

Persistent rules may constrain or standardize coding-AI behavior.
They may not create new external or irreversible authority.

---

## 11. Revocation Boundary

For v0.1:

```text
Prior Verified Save / Verified Reuse history
→ preserved

Future use of the revoked Repository Default
→ stopped
```

Revocation does not rewrite or delete prior facts.

The following remain parked until the Never Again lifecycle is designed:

- effect on displayed unlock state;
- effect on related active rules;
- reset;
- recount;
- invalidation taxonomy;
- re-approval behavior;
- current-active-count display.

These parked lifecycle questions must not delay the first Verified Save vertical slice.

---

## 12. Receipt

A local Receipt for Verified Save or Verified Reuse must record at least:

- repository identity;
- decision identity;
- original save event;
- later Run identity;
- reuse event;
- skipped-interruption result;
- Wrapper checkpoint result;
- override result;
- Verified Save / Verified Reuse classification;
- As-of timestamp.

A Receipt is evidence, not authority.

---

## 13. Evidence Boundary

Verified Save is:

> local proof-of-use recorded by the repository.

It is not:

- third-party certification;
- externally authenticated evidence;
- Sybil-resistant proof;
- universal productivity proof;
- safety certification;
- proof of repository authenticity;
- proof that synthetic-repository gaming is technically prevented.

The local-only design remains effectively honor-based even with strict
anti-inflation rules.

This limitation must be disclosed honestly.

Recovered-time, interruption, and cost figures are estimates.
They do not determine Verified Save status or unlock.

---

## 14. Fable Boundary

Fable is:

- a pre-release independent adversarial Audit Seat;
- an optional advanced route;
- evidence of how the release was challenged.

Fable is not:

- a runtime dependency for ordinary users;
- required for Verified Save;
- required for Never Again Mode unlock;
- a subscription ordinary users must purchase;
- third-party certification;
- proof of universal safety.

---

## 15. Public Wording Boundary

Candidate public description:

> Save a repository decision once.  
> When it reappears in a later Run, Companion can reuse it without asking again.  
> Five distinct Verified Saves in the same repository unlock Never Again Mode.

Japanese:

> リポジトリ判断を一度保存すると、後の別Runで同じ判断が必要になった際、
> Companionは同じ質問を繰り返さずに再利用できます。  
> 同一リポジトリで五つの異なるVerified Saveが成立すると、
> Never Again Modeが解放されます。

The line:

> One AI builds it. Another tries to break it.  
> What survives becomes reusable control.

must not be published until an actual evidence chain exists:

```text
Pro Design
→ Codex implementation
→ Companion role / identity / evidence fixation
→ independent Fable audit
→ Shin ACCEPT / REJECT / PARK
→ accepted Forward-only repair
→ post-repair evidence
```

---

## 16. v0.1 CAP Boundary

### Included

- Companion ordinary-user route;
- Repository Defaults from first use;
- Verified Save;
- Verified Reuse;
- local Receipts;
- bounded recovery estimates;
- repository-local 5-save progress;
- Never Again Mode unlock;
- human-approved repository-rule candidates;
- future-use revocation;
- local-proof disclosure.

### Parked

- user-global unlock;
- cross-repository unlock;
- clone / fork inheritance;
- reset / recount / invalidation lifecycle;
- autonomous rule activation;
- automatic merge / release / publication;
- multiple unlock features;
- hosted audit;
- Fable runtime API;
- portable verification credentials;
- Sybil resistance;
- public leaderboards;
- universal savings formulas.

---

## 17. First Implementation Slice

After Companion fixation and approved Pro Design, the first implementation must be
limited to one vertical slice:

```text
1. Human selects Use for this repository
2. Repository Default is saved
3. A later, separate Run begins
4. The same decision identity reappears
5. The Default is included in the coding-AI packet
6. The coding AI reuses it
7. The repeated human question is skipped
8. Wrapper-owned checkpoint passes
9. Verified Save Receipt is recorded
```

Do not implement the Never Again rule engine, reset lifecycle, clone/fork
inheritance, runtime Fable route, or additional unlocks before this slice passes.

---

# Companion Fixation Instruction

Companion now owns only the fixation of this approved Product Contract.

Companion must:

1. preserve the Contract wording and boundaries;
2. assign stable identity, role, As-of, evidence, and authority fields;
3. identify any internal contradiction without redesigning the route;
4. generate one exact Copy-for-Pro packet for the existing canonical Codex thread;
5. keep Codex / Pro / Fable / implementation on HOLD until Shin authorizes the
   generated packet;
6. expose only the next required action.

Companion must not:

- add new unlock features;
- redesign Verified Save;
- make Fable an ordinary-user dependency;
- convert local evidence into third-party verification;
- invent reset, recount, invalidation, clone, fork, or portability semantics;
- authorize implementation;
- return routine formatting or routing cleanup to Shin.

# Completion Line for Companion Fixation

Companion fixation is complete only when it produces:

- fixed Contract identity;
- fixed role and authority boundary;
- fixed As-of and evidence boundary;
- exact Copy-for-Pro packet;
- explicit HOLD on all downstream execution.

No repository modification, Codex execution, Pro Design, Fable audit, release, or
publication is authorized by this artifact.
